body: U+0023# What produced this threadU+000AU+000AA read-only investigation of a performance incident, then a report, then the SPEC this thread implements. No configuration was changed.U+000AU+000AU+002A*The incident.** One session drove a 26-part programme through `delivery-lead` subagents, each dispatching its own makers and reviewers. In 9 hours of wall clock, 6 of 26 units completed.U+000AU+000AU+002A*The mechanism, in three steps.** `rules/common/agents.md:17` and `agents/delivery-lead.md:91` told every Lead that its children die when it ends its turn and that no way exists to wait. Four lines above, `:89` and `:95` made ending the turn equivalent to abandoning the unit. So each Lead held its turn open with the only blocking primitive it had — `sleep` in the shell — and 458 minutes went into deliberate waiting, 86% of all Bash time.U+000AU+000AU+002A*The claim is false.** A live experiment settled it: a parent dispatched one child and stopped at 18:09:21; the child ran to completion at 18:11:27, 124 seconds later, and its result was delivered upward automatically. The harness said so in the text of all 55 dispatch results ("You will be notified automatically when it completes"), and 143 completion notifications were delivered into subagents during the incident, 19 of them into a Lead that slept through them. 149 minutes of the sleeping happened after the awaited answer had already arrived.U+000AU+000AU+002A*What else the measurement found**U+000AU+000AU+002D The coordination layer of 13 Leads cost 701 agent-minutes and 24.7M tokens; the 55 workers cost 547 minutes and 22.0M.U+000AU+002D An agent that does nothing at all costs 53,820 to 77,727 tokens. The cheapest real dispatch in the incident cost 137,191 against a declared "~5-10k".U+000AU+002D Parents wrote 124,101 tokens of briefs across 37 maker dispatches, all landing permanently in the parent's own context.U+000AU+002D One Lead never slept and instead re-read the same task output file 224 times, burning 314.7M cache-read tokens — 31% of the session — across 1,184 turns.U+000AU+002D 13 of 68 agents were rework, 221 minutes, 18% of all agent time, triggered by MEDIUM/LOW findings and by findings about whether tests could go red.U+000AU+002D Agent reasoning is not recoverable: 2,318 thinking blocks exist and every one has zero-length text.U+000AU+000AU+002A*Three systems explain refusals by naming the wrong cause.** The logbook `record_decision` refusal describes a maxItems problem for an `options` field that was simply absent (12 occurrences). The `SendMessage` refusal says "disabled for this session" when the tool is merely outside that agent's grant — 23 sessions contain both verdicts at once. And the configuration itself asserts a harness limitation that is not one. Same failure shape at three scales.U+000AU+000AU+002A*Verification cost of the investigation:** nine probe agents, roughly 617,000 tokens. The incident session was still running throughout and its totals moved during analysis, from 68 agents to 77 and from 348 to 458 minutes of waiting.U+000A
